claim: The fossil used to identify it – a partial braincase – has been lying in the archives of the Natural History Museum in London since it was acquired from a Reverend Reginald Hooley in 1924.
label: PARTIALLY_TRUE
annotatorNote: [AI label: Claude, 2026-10-14 - not yet checked by the human annotator] Need a look. The central claim holds: the specimen (back of the skull, Invictibellatrix amberina, Royal Society Open Science) was acquired by the Natural History Museum in 1924 and lay unstudied (Phys.org, 13 Oct 2026). A detail does not: Reginald Walter Hooley was a wine merchant and amateur palaeontologist, not a clergyman, and he died on 5 May 1923 - the museum acquired his collection in 1924, after his death, not from him. Possibly confused with the Rev. William Fox, the Victorian Isle of Wight collector (a guess).
